newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ budget surplus in 8 mths to Feb above forecast.
newsitem.headline: NZ budget surplus in 8 mths to Feb above forecast.

text.p: The New Zealand government said on Thursday it posted a NZ$2.257 billion operating budget surplus for the eight months to February 28, 1997, against a forecast surplus of $2.092 billion.
Net public debt as a percentage of GDP was 27.9 percent at February 28 against 29.1 percent at December 31, 1996.
Treasury said several factors were behind the improved operating result.
Non-tax revenue was $93 million or 5.3 percent above forecast. Expenses, excluding net foreign exchange gains, were $139 million or 0.6 percent lower than forecast.
In addition, the net surplus (less distributions) attributable to State-owned enterprises and Crown entities was $70 million (14.4 percent) greater than forecast.
Partly offsetting these favourable variances was taxation revenue that was $116 million (0.5 percent) lower than forecast.

Treasury said the year-to-date favourable variance in the operating balance had reduced by $73 million in the month of February, due primarily to tax revenue falling by $162 million against forecast in the month.
The government's net worth stood at $5.863 billion against a forecast $5.642 billion and compared with $5.484 billion at December 31.
The improvement in the net worth was mainly due to the higher than forecast operating surplus of $2.257 billion and net asset revaluations of $262 million.

Net public debt was $376 million lower than forecast at $25.71 billion, mainly due to lower than forecast net purchases of physical assets ($316 million) and stronger than forecast net cash flows from operations ($28 million).
Net cash flows from operating and investing activities were $4.25 billion, compared with a forecast inflow of $4.337 billion. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
